stories.headline: Man City owners must sell due to 'shame of their guilt' - Jamie Carragher
stories.summary: Manchester City's owners must sell up in the wake of the club's guilty verdict for breaching Premier League financial rules, according to former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher.
stories.body:
Manchester City's owners must sell up in the wake of the club's guilty verdict for breaching Premier League financial rules, according to former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher.

Carragher says there can be no future for any executives implicated in the scandal, which City have stressed they intend to appeal, from majority owner Sheikh Mansour downwards.

An independent commission concluded City "clearly intended to circumvent Premier League rules" by inflating revenue and hiding costs through a series of "sham" commercial deals over a nine-season period.

Writing in the Daily Telegraph, Carragher said: "Manchester City are the end of their Abu Dhabi era. The club can only heal and recover from the shame of their guilt once the custodians recognise they have failed in their duty and sell up.

"There is no way to sugar-coat this. The scale of the institutional cheating and lack of co-operation in the investigation means the position of all City executives involved is untenable.

"Fighting on will only prolong the agony of supporters who wrong believe their pleas of innocence."

Carragher's views appear to contradict those of Prime Minister Andy Burnham, who suggested on Wednesday that such a sanction may not be suited to a group who have pumped billions into the club since their arrival in the city in 2008.

Burnham, the former mayor of Greater Manchester, told the BBC: "I would be really concerned to lose them.

"They've been such a huge partner in the building of modern Manchester. Obviously, the building of Manchester City into the global force that it is."

Burnham's comments came after David Kogan, chair of the Independent Football Regulator (IFR) said the ruling "raises serious issues" and pointed out the body has the power to assess the suitability of club owners and executives once proceedings come to a close.

Carragher is adamant there must be no mercy shown to those proven to have been complicit in one of the game's greatest controversies, and that any failure to uphold the rules will render such powers obsolete.

He added: "The Premier League's owners' and directors' test makes clear the repercussions for breaking the fundamental rules that all member clubs, including City, established and signed up to.

"Anyone who falls short must be disqualified from being Premier League directors and owners; otherwise, the regulations are not fit for purpose."

City have shown every intention of rigorously contesting the charges, and in a further development on Wednesday, the club's main sponsor Etihad Airways released a statement saying it was assessing its legal options following the independent commission's ruling.

- Klopp not preparing for more titles after verdict against Man City

- UK PM Burnham 'concerned' Man City's owners could sell club

- Erling Haaland unaffected by Man City guilty verdict, says Norway teammate

The club have the support of former manager Pep Guardiola, who won six Premier League titles with City before leaving at the end of last season.

Guardiola wrote on social media: "I want every single @ManCity fan to know I am here; more than ever.

"I am, always have been, always will, be behind my club, my owner, my chairman, Ferran, the players, staff, Enzo and you, our unique supporters.

"Let me be clear: we will get through this together. I love you all."

stories.headline: Max Verstappen steps in for GT race at Portimão amid two F1 triple-headers
stories.summary: This weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia will be the second of seven consecutive race weekends for Max Verstappen after he confirmed he has added a GT race at Portimão to his schedule for later this month.
stories.body:
This weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia will be the second of seven consecutive race weekends for Max Verstappen after he confirmed he has added a GT race at Portimão to his schedule for later this month.

Verstappen's GT team, Verstappen Racing, is participating in the GT World Challenge this year, but two of its drivers, Dani Juncadella and Jules Gounon, have a World Endurance Championship calendar clash with the Portuguese round on Oct. 18.

The race at Portimão does not clash with an F1 weekend -- falling between the Singapore Grand Prix and U.S. Grand Prix -- and Verstappen has confirmed he will step in to make sure his team has a full driver line-up.

"I know that two of my drivers won't be part of the line-up, so two other drivers need to step in and I'm looking forward to it," he said.

"It's going to be a busy seven weeks, but we'll do it and I enjoy it anyway. So, yeah. Let's see what we can do there."

F1 is in the midst of one of its most intense periods of races in its 76-year history, with this weekend's race in Malaysia the second of nine scheduled grands prix in 11 weeks.

The Bahrain Grand Prix was originally meant to go ahead in April, but was cancelled due to the ongoing conflict between the United States and Iran in the region.

Rather than scrap the round altogether, Bahrain and F1 came to an agreement with Malaysia to host the race 4,000 miles away at the Sepang International Circuit this weekend.

- Why is the Bahrain Grand Prix taking place in Malaysia, 4,000 miles away? F1's unusual race explained

- Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia: Where were today's drivers when F1 last raced at Sepang?

- Fernando Alonso refuses to watch F1 from the sofa while he still has 'fire' inside to do better

When asked how he was coping with the upcoming flurry of races, Verstappen joked that his apathy towards F1's controversial power unit regulations this year had made it easier to get in the right headspace.

"I think I had four or five months of very intense preparation -- deep mental preparation of not giving an F," he said with a smile on his face. "So, yeah, I just rock up."

Verstappen also raced for his GT team at this year's Nürburgring 24 Hours, which he has since referenced as the highlight of his 2026 season to date.

His best results in F1 this year have been four second place finishes in Austria, Hungary, Spain and Azerbaijan, but he remains hopeful he can go one better and win a grand prix before the end of 2026.

"I'm trying everything I can," he said. "We are scoring, of course, quite a few podiums now, but I want to win. That's what I'm here for.

"And I'm getting close, but I want to at least win one race this year. So I hope we can do it, of course, at some point. But yeah, we have some solid results."

stories.headline: White Sox pounce early, finish sweep of Astros for first playoff series win since 2005
stories.summary: — From 100 losses to their first playoff series win in two decades, these scrappy Chicago White Sox just keep outdoing themselves.
stories.body:
HOUSTON -- — From 100 losses to their first playoff series win in two decades, these scrappy Chicago White Sox just keep outdoing themselves.


The White Sox used a big first inning and a three-run homer from Chase Meidroth to propel them to a 7-3 win over the Houston Astros on Wednesday to sweep their AL Wild Card Series.


“I’m proud of the guys and certainly happy for them as they’re probably the only ones in this country that believed that they could be in this spot," manager Will Venable said. “And they maintained that belief in the beginning of the season and went throughout the season maintaining that, and they made it happen. So it’s awesome to get to this point.”


It's the first time Chicago has won a playoff series since beating Houston in the World Series in 2005. Under the direction of Venable, the second-year skipper, and with a letter of support from Pope Leo XIV, the White Sox advanced to face AL Central champion Cleveland in the AL Division Series beginning Saturday in Cleveland.


“It means everything for our fans,” Meidroth said. “They have been incredible all year. So the main thing was getting back to Chicago for some postseason baseball, and so we’re really blessed that we get to do that.”


The White Sox, who lost 100 games in each of the last three seasons, are the only team in major league history to follow consecutive 100-loss seasons with a playoff berth.


The AL West-winning Astros went 81-81 to become the first team to reach the postseason without a winning record. Their recent playoff woes in Houston continued Wednesday as they dropped their ninth straight home playoff game in a ninth trip to the postseason in the last 10 years.


Chicago pounced on the Astros for four runs in the first inning a day after scoring three in the first two innings of a 6-3 win. Houston ace Hunter Brown was lifted after getting just two outs and wasn’t helped by a sloppy defense which committed two first-inning errors.


He was 6-0 with a 2.39 ERA in six career starts against the White Sox before Wednesday’s debacle.


The Astros clawed their way back into it with solo home runs from Jeremy Peña, Cam Smith and Jose Altuve to trail by 1 entering the sixth inning.


AJ Blubaugh, who opened Game 1, and Peter Lambert, pitching on two days’ rest, combined to retire the next 13 batters after Brown exited. Chicago’s next baserunner came when Lambert walked Andrew Benintendi to start the sixth and then walked Tristan Peters.


Bryan Abreu came in, and Meidroth smashed his fifth pitch off the wall in left field to push the lead to 7-3. He yelled on his entire trip around the bases to the delight of a patch of White Sox fans seated near the visitor’s dugout.


“I was looking for something middle up,” Meidroth said. “He’s had my number all year, really good fastball, so I got something middle up and I was able to cash in for the team. So, yeah, that was awesome.”


Houston faced boos for a second game in a row from an unusually thin crowd. It’s a second straight playoff trip where the Astros have been swept at home in the wild card after losing both games to Detroit in 2024.


Now they’ll face an uncertain future with manager Joe Espada’s contract set to expire at season’s end after general manager Dana Brown was fired last month.


“We fought back and we set our goal to win this division and we accomplished that,” Espada said. “We wanted to play deep in October. We came short on that. But just the way our guys stayed together and were able to get this far, extremely proud of our team.”


It was a disappointing series for Houston slugger and AL MVP-favorite Yordan Alvarez, who managed only a single with two strikeouts in eight at-bats in the series.


Altuve’s shot to the seats in left field in the fourth inning got the Astros within 4-3. It was the 28th postseason homer of his career, which is second in MLB history behind Manny Ramirez (29).


“We’re all sad,” Altuve said. “We wanted to go to the World Series and win it. But today is sorrow for the final day of the season."


The Astros had a shot to take the lead before Meidroth’s homer. They loaded the bases with two outs in the fifth, but Anthony Kay retired Altuve on a fly out to end the inning.

stories.headline: AFL player movement tracker: trade requests, free agency latest, who's on the move?
stories.summary: The offseason is upon us which means AFL trades, free agency, and player movement is about to take off. Here's the latest news, whispers, and confirmed deals.
stories.body:
It's AFL player movement season, with trades and free agency set to dominate the month of October. So who is going where? Keep track with our player movement guide here.

When is the AFL trade and free agency window?
The 2026 AFL trade period commences on Monday, October 5 and closes in the evening of Wednesday, October 14.

The free agency window opens and closes a little ealier; it runs from Friday, October 2 until Friday, October 9.

Thursday, Oct. 1

Goater set to make cross-city switch

North Melbourne defender Josh Goater is set to join the Hawks after requesting a trade on Thursday.

Having played just 18 games, the 23-year-old had fallen out of favour after an injury-hit run in his time at North.

Premiership Lion requests trade

The Brisbane Lions have confirmed Sam Marshall has requested a trade to St Kilda.

"The Brisbane Lions confirm premiership midfielder Sam Marshall has requested to be traded to St Kilda," the Lions said in a statement.

"Marshall has played 13 games, including the 2025 Premiership, across two seasons since being selected in the first round of the 2024 draft as a graduate of the Youi Brisbane Lions Academy.

"The club respects Marshall's request to be traded, and will work towards facilitating an outcome that best reflects true value to the Brisbane Lions for the 20-year-old."

Tuesday, Sept. 29
Neale informs Lions he intends to join Collingwood

Two-time Brownlow Medal winner Lachie Neale has told Brisbane he will depart the club as an unrestricted free agent and sign a three-year deal with Collingwood.

Aware that Neale intended to leave at the end of the year, the Lions never offered him a new contract.

The paperwork for the deal is expected to be formalised as early as Friday when the free agency period opens.

Friday, Sept. 25
Jordon Butts to join the Bulldogs

Zak Butters isn't the only South Australian-based player keen to join the Western Bulldogs, with Crows' key defender Jordon Butts officially naming the Dogs as his preferred offseason destination.

The unrestricted free agent will sign a five-year deal at the Kennel, according to AFL.com.au.

Tuesday, Sept. 22
Amartey officially names Carlton

Wantaway Sydney forward Joel Amartey has confirmed his desire to join Carlton as an unrestricted free agent.

The 26-year-old was kept out of the Swans' side with an Achilles injury in the latter stages of the year.

With Charlie Curnow (75 goals in 2026) and Logan McDonald (51) cementing their spots in the Sydney forward line as the prime targets, Amartey is hoping for more opportunity at the Blues.

Thursday, Sept. 17
GWS captain finally makes big call on his future

Toby Greene has opted to leave GWS, telling the AFL club he wishes to play with Geelong next season. Greene, who has been at the Giants since their foundation season in 2012, wants to go back to Victoria for family reasons.

In an extraordinary way to announce the decision, outgoing GWS boss Dave Matthews confirmed Greene's intentions on radio, before the club released a statement.

The 32-year-old has been offered a lucrative three-year deal to join the Cats.

Saturday, Sept. 12
Zak Butters makes huge free agency call
The year's hottest restricted free agent Zak Butters has made a huge call on his future, nominating the Western Bulldogs as his preferred destination.

After a year of speculation, with Geelong thought to be the front-runner for the Power star's signature, Butters made the call on Saturday, first reported by AFL.com.au's Callum Twomey.

The deal is reportedly for nine years.

Thursday, Sept. 10
Hogan set to join Pies
GWS and Collingwood have both confirmed that 2024 Coleman Medal winner Jesse Hogan has chosen the Magpies at his next home.

Set to be a four-club player, Hogan is 31 and coming off a 12-goal season from just nine appearances.

It's a big boost for the Magpies if Hogan can recapture his form; key forward has been an area of concern for a number of years.

Tuesday, Sept. 8
Bailey set to be Lion for life
Brisbane's Zac Bailey has ended months of 'will he, won't he' speculation to sign with the Lions for eight years, taking him through the 2034 season, the the club confirmed on Tuesday.

Bailey, a free agent, had been a big target for the Crows, who had reportedly tabled a more lucrative offer.

"I'm absolutely rapt to be staying at the Brisbane Lions," Bailey said in a statement.

"I love the environment here, the players, coaches and staff who all make it a great place to be and I feel like this Club continues to bring the best out of me.

"This Club means so much to me - I came here as a young player and have grown up here and to know I will be here long-term is something I'm really proud of.

"I would like to thank the club, my partner Em, my family and my management for being so supportive throughout this process.

"I love what we as a club have achieved during my time here and I am super excited about what we can continue to achieve together."

Rowan Marshall requests trade
St Kilda ruck Rowan Marshall looks set to be on the move, with the Saints confirming the big man had requested a trade for the second straight season.

While Marshall hasn't requested a specific club, it's likely to be Geelong after he failed to secure a trade to the Cats last year. He played 21 games for the Saints this seaosn, juggling ruck duties with Tom De Koning, who came in from Carlton last offseason.

"Rowan is a highly valued member of the St Kilda Football Club and remains contracted until the end of 2027," the Saints said in a statement.

"Marshall has not nominated a preferred destination at this stage, with the club making clear that any trade will need to be in the best interests of the St Kilda Football Club."

Zane Duursma wants to go to Melbourne
The No. 4 pick in the 2023 AFL draft Zane Duursma has requested a trade out of North Melbourne, with Melbourne in his sights.

The news comes a week after coach Alastair Clarkson was sacked by the club. North won nine games in 2026, their best return since 2019.

Ed Allan re-signs with the Pies
After speculation about his future at the Magpies, mdifielder Ed Allan has put pen to paper, signing a four year extension to remain at Collingwood.

2026 was a breakout season for Allan, who played 19 games and averaged a career-high 16.5 disposals per game.

Monday, Sept. 7
Pair of in-demand Dogs re-sign
According to afl.com.au, both Arty Jones and Buku Khamis will remain at the Kennel this offseason.

Jones will sign a three-year deal, while Khamis has a five-year contract in front of him.

Essendon and Brisbane had interest in livewire forward Jones, who had a standout performance against Collingwood in the wildcard final win, while the Blues were heavily linked to Khamis for a second straight offseason.

Cooper Hodge nomintes Hawthorn
A big boost for the Hawks, with club champion Luke Hodge's son Cooper choosing to join the Melbourne-based team as a father-son at this year's draft.

He had the option of going to Brisbane as a Lions academy member.

stories.headline: Wings' Ogunbowale scores record 45 to force Game 3 vs. Valkyries
stories.summary: Arike Ogunbowale delivered a record-breaking performance with the Wings' season on the line, scoring 45 points, including a tying 3-pointer to force overtime, to help Dallas force a deciding Game 3 against the Valkyries.
stories.body:
ARLINGTON, Texas -- Arike Ogunbowale stood near Paige Bueckers and waited for the star guard to make a move on her dribble with the Dallas Wings trailing by three as the final seconds of regulation -- and their season -- ticked away.

Bueckers waved toward her backcourt mate, but she wasn't telling Ogunbowale to get out of the way. She was telling her to get open.

After all, Bueckers knew whom the hot hand was -- and it wasn't her.

Ogunbowale took a pass from Bueckers on the left baseline, dribbled toward the corner and hit an off-balance corner 3-pointer, sending the game to overtime and her on the way to a WNBA playoff-record 45 points as the Wings won a thriller 108-100 on Wednesday night, forcing a Game 3 in their first-round series.

The deciding game will be Friday night in San Francisco, where the Valkyries won the series opener by 24 points.

Golden State is trying to advance in the playoffs for the first time in the franchise's second season. The Wings are trying to reach the semifinals for the second time in six postseason appearances since moving to the Dallas area in 2016.

Ogunbowale opened the extra period of Game 2 by banking in a 3, then hit another one to put Dallas ahead for good at 103-100 with 1:46 remaining. A four-time All-Star, she easily topped her previous playoff best of 24 points after scoring 10 points on just seven shots in the series opener.

"We felt like we got pushed around out there when we played in San Francisco, and especially me, personally, I don't feel like I was aggressive," Ogunbowale said. "I didn't know what I would score. I was going to shoot regardless because I just feel like seven shots isn't enough to win playoffs and I have to be aggressive whether it's going in or not."

Bueckers, the 2025 No. 1 overall pick and Rookie of the Year who is in her first playoff series, was mired in a 3-for-13 shooting night that included an air ball on a 3-pointer with the Wings trailing by three in the final two minutes of regulation. But she assisted on Ogunbowale's tying 3, and again on a the banked 3 to start OT. Bueckers finished with 10 points and had four assists.

"For us to do what we did today without Paige having the type of game that she always has offensively for us, to come out with a win is huge," Wings coach Jose Fernandez said. "We had other people step up."

Ogunbowale's shot for a 93-93 tie with 4.1 seconds left in regulation of Game 2 was followed by Gabby Williams getting called for an offensive foul on the inbound play after a Golden State timeout.

That call was reversed on replay, so instead of Aziaha James having a chance to give Dallas the lead at the free throw line, there was a jump ball at center court with 3.0 seconds to go. After a scramble for the loose ball, Golden State's desperation shot was way off target and after the buzzer.

Williams scored 36 points, a career-high for regular season or playoffs, but she missed all six of her shots in the final 1:31 of overtime to finish 12-of-23 from the field.

"We got one at home, and we got to bring our best," Valkyries coach Natalie Nakase said. "That was not our best. Tomorrow's got to be clear minds, clear focus, clear game plan, and then be ready to go for the game at home."

Ogunbowale scored 22 points in the fourth quarter and overtime -- 11 in each period. She passed her previous overall career high of 41 points with the 3 that put Dallas up for good.

Dallas' Alysha Clark tied her playoff career high with 21 points, and Aziaha James added 13.

Kaila Charles scored 14 points for the Valkyries, and Kayla Thornton had 13.

With the scored tied at 98 in the extra period, Ogunbowale and Tiffany Hayes had to be separated after making contact. Both were called for flagrant fouls, and each made a pair of free throws with 2:26 remaining.

The Valkyries didn't score again, shooting 2-of-12 in overtime.

stories.headline: Sources: Steelers to trade Joey Porter Jr. to Cowboys
stories.summary: The Steelers agreed to trade cornerback Joey Porter Jr. to the Cowboys for a 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second-rounder, sources confirmed to ESPN on Wednesday night.
stories.body:
After a lengthy and contentious contract standoff and a lingering back issue, Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. is going to the Dallas Cowboys.

The Steelers on Wednesday night agreed to trade Porter to the Cowboys for a 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second-rounder, sources told ESPN.

The trade marks the end of a monthslong saga that stretched throughout the Steelers' offseason as Porter, one of the team's 2023 second-round picks, awaited an extension and was sidelined by a back injury.

The heart of the dispute was the guaranteed money within the contract's structure, sources told ESPN, and the sides never made meaningful progress on agreeing to terms despite talks as late as hours before kickoff of the Steelers' Week 1 game against the Atlanta Falcons. The Steelers then stopped talks because they don't negotiate during the regular season as a longstanding organizational principle.

Porter, who started 41 games and had three interceptions in three seasons, sat out all of the team's training camp and preseason after reporting an aggravation to the back injury during the team's mobility workout on the first day of camp. He was put on the physically unable to perform list until roster cutdown day in late August.

Porter was then a limited participant in every regular-season practice until earlier this week as coach Mike McCarthy said the cornerback was progressing through a "ramp-up" phase during the first month of the season.

Porter was inactive for each of the first three games and had been ruled out earlier Wednesday of the Steelers' game Thursday night against the Browns in Cleveland. The Steelers added a back injury to Wednesday's practice report in addition to the "not injury related-conditioning" description the team used for Porter's injury status for most of the past three weeks. Porter had previously been a full participant in the team's Monday and Tuesday walkthroughs.

His departure means the Steelers will continue to operate with Asante Samuel Jr., Jamel Dean and Daylen Everette rotating at outside cornerback. Everette, a 2026 third-round draft pick, played extended snaps in a Week 3 win against the Cincinnati Bengals, first coming in for a briefly injured Dean and then replacing Samuel for much of the second half.

Cowboys owner and general manager Jerry Jones hinted during training camp that he would be willing to give up draft capital to help this season's team. Jones was asked on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas on Monday about a potential trade with reports of the team's interest in Porter.

While not specifically talking about Porter because of tampering rules, Jones said, "I'd just say we're right on top of it. We're very aware of the moving parts out here."

The Cowboys have had a need for cornerback help with Cobie Durant expected to sit out his second game because of a hamstring strain. In last weekend's loss to the Baltimore Ravens, Durant's replacement, Shavon Revel, injured his knee and ankle. He was limited in Wednesday's practice. Revel sat out the first eight games of his rookie season recovering from a torn ACL in his right knee sustained while at East Carolina, but the current injury is to his left knee.

At the end of the game against the Ravens, the Cowboys used backups Caelen Carson and Ameer Speed opposite DaRon Bland with Reddy Steward, a practice squad call-up, working the slot.

This is the third trade between the Cowboys and Steelers in the past two years. In May 2025, the Cowboys sent a 2026 third-round pick and a 2027 fifth-rounder to Pittsburgh for wide receiver George Pickens and a 2027 sixth-round pick.

In August, the Cowboys acquired tackle Broderick Jones and a 2027 fourth-rounder for third- and sixth-round picks in 2027.

The Ringer first reported news of the Porter trade.

stories.headline: St. Louis up to 2nd place with unbeaten run now at 17 games
stories.summary: Simon Becher and Tomas Ostrak each scored late in the second half as St. Louis City SC beat the New York Red Bulls 3-0 on Wednesday night.
stories.body:
Simon Becher and Tomas Ostrak each scored late in the second half as St. Louis City SC beat the New York Red Bulls 3-0 on Wednesday night.

St. Louis (13-6-8) extended its unbeaten streak to 17 matches in MLS play and moved up to second place in MLS' Western Conference table.

New York (9-12-6) entered having conceded just two goals in its last four games, with Ethan Horvath recording three shutouts.

The Red Bulls had won their last two games, but were without rising stars Adri Mehmeti and Julian Hall for the game, with the pair away on national team duty for the United States.

Rafael Navarro opened the scoring just five minutes into the game when he redirected Conrad Wallem's header across the goal.

Becher capitalized on a New York turnover deep in its own half to make it 2-0 in the 87th minute. Ostrak sent in a rebound in stoppage time.

Roman Bürki made four saves to earn his third clean sheet of the season for St. Louis.

It was the first time New York and St. Louis have met during the regular season.

St. Louis hosts the LA Galaxy next on Oct. 11, while the Red Bulls play San Diego FC at home the day before.

stories.headline: 76ers guard Tyrese Maxey: 'I want to be judged by winning'
stories.summary: Coming off a career year, Tyrese Maxey said he doesn't want to be judged by how he does individually but by how the 76ers do as a team this year.
stories.body:
CAMDEN, N.J. -- Having earned two All-Star nods in the last three seasons and coming off a campaign in which he averaged a career-high 28.3 points per game, Philadelphia 76ers guard Tyrese Maxey is primed for another big year.

But the 25-year-old said Wednesday after the Sixers' second practice of training camp that the only metric he cares about for Philadelphia's highly anticipated upcoming season is team success.

"I'm at the point now where I've showed what I can do talent-wise," Maxey said. "Of course, I'm going to continue to get better, but I want to be judged by winning. If we win, that's what I want to be judged by. That's really my main mindset, my main goal, is finding ways to win."

Maxey was the first of Philly's four major stars -- including Joel Embiid, Jaylen Brown and LeBron James -- to speak to reporters since training camp started Tuesday.

Brown sidestepped a query on media day Monday when asked about how the Sixers will determine a pecking order and identify an "alpha" by replying: "Next question."

Maxey's answer was in the same spirit, albeit much more elaborate, as he detailed his willingness to adjust to help the team.

"Because I've played so many different roles, I'm capable of doing so many different things," Maxey said. "And I think that's going to be a positive for myself and for this team. I can play on the ball. I can play off the ball. I can play in transition. I can catch and shoot. Play off [of] pin downs. I can play pick-and-roll. ...

"I'm going to play however they need me to play. However Coach [Nick Nurse] wants to play, that's how I'm going to play."

And Maxey is not only leading by example. He is speaking up as the new group gets off the ground.

"My voice carries a little bit and then just the charisma of me smiling and having a good time," Maxey said. "I mean, I'm getting older ... and I just feel like I've been here for a minute. Process [Embiid] has been here, I think what, 13 years? I've been here seven. So, we've been here for a while, kind of know how things go around here and just am trying to keep using my voice and help everybody get familiar and help everybody get comfortable."

Beyond vowing to acquiesce to any role change that is asked of him, Maxey also used his voice to be effusive in his praise of the other stars on the team in his answers Wednesday.

On James: "That's like a big brother to me. He's an old man ... He's a good guy. He's a good guy."

On Embiid: "He looks amazing. He looks happy. ... When you're healthy and you're happy and you're at peace with your life and basketball, that's when you're at your best. He's been great."

On Brown: "JB's like physically a freak of nature. He's just stronger than you. He jumps higher than you. He's faster than you and he's very talented. Those are the things that you see every single day. And I think what's stood out to me so far is his communication and he's willing to pick up the ball defensively, kind of just do whatever coach needs him to do right now."

Brown was the last player on the court after practice, working on handling double teams in the post - by kicking out to a shooter or fading away for a jumper along the baseline - with a massive Sixers logo on the wall of the practice facility behind him.

Maxey made sure to acknowledge the transition for Brown, too, as he begins life with the Sixers after having played for the Boston Celtics for his entire career before being traded within the Atlantic Division in July.

"This is very foreign to him, imagine being somewhere for [10] years and coming here, the team that you're trained to hate, probably," Maxey said. "It's been great. Especially [since] we just beat [Boston in the playoffs]. It's kind of crazy."

stories.headline: Ivan: Nathan Cleary can get even better after Dally M
stories.summary: Ivan Cleary has spoken of the horror of watching his son Nathan's leg injury, and a belief he can still get better again after winning his first Dally M.
stories.body:
Ivan Cleary has admitted watching his son Nathan suffer a badly broken leg marked one of the hardest days of his career, feeling the line between father and coach blurred for the first time.

But the veteran Penrith mentor is insistent his son Nathan still has more levels to attain once he returns from his injury, following his landmark Dally M victory on Wednesday night.

Cleary's Dally M triumph completed the Penrith halfback's rugby league box set, having now claimed every major team and individual honour available to him by age 28.

Unable to attend in person after being released from hospital following emergency surgery on his leg, the Panthers halfback collected the game's top honour while in a wheelchair at home.

Coach Ivan also appeared emotional during Nathan's pre-recorded speech, after the trophy was hand-delivered to the halfback earlier in the day.

"His voice perked up from what it's been the past couple of days," Ivan told AAP.

"It's a pretty amazing award. You don't play the game for individual awards, but it's certainly nice to be recognised.

"Particularly this award, it's pretty much the No.1 award in the game."

Reminded that his son had now scaled virtually every possible mountain in the sport, the Penrith coach insisted there were still improvements left in his son's game.

"It's crazy," Ivan said.

"I know he'd say it and I probably think a bit the same. You don't reflect too much when it's still going on. But when you put it like that, it's amazing.

"But I know there is so much more to come as well, and I know he thinks that way as well."

Nathan has received positive early news from surgeons after the operation on his compound fracture and dislocated ankle, as a result of a hip-drop tackle in Sunday's preliminary-final loss to Newcastle.

He will soon undergo surgery on other foot after fighting through a broken bone to play the Knights, but Penrith are hopeful he will be right for round one in 2027.

"Sunday was definitely one of the harder days I have been through," coach Cleary said.

"It's the first time where the line of dad and coach got a bit blurred. And the loss, I guess we have had a lot of good days so you can't have it all your way.

"Very emotional, but life goes on."

Footage has also emerged of fullback Dylan Edwards not only being horrified by the graphic injury at first, but then also trying to stop Nathan from seeing it.

"I was just trying to keep him calm as I could," Edwards said.

"To his credit he is a tough person. And the way he was handling that was incredible.

"It was gut-wrenching, something you're not used to seeing on the footy field."

Edwards, meanwhile, is still hopeful of being able to represent Australia at the World Cup after avoiding knee surgery following a PCL injury in the loss.

"I'm not sure, I have to talk to Kevvie (coach Kevin Walters)," Edwards said, while wearing a brace at the Dally Ms.

stories.headline: Which Premier League players got injured in the international break?
stories.summary: All the latest news and updates on Premier League stars injuries during the first international break of the 2026-2027 club season
stories.body:
Premier League teams will be watching and hoping their star players remain healthy throughout the international break.

However, some have already sustained injuries while playing for their countries. Premier League matches resume on Oct. 10.

ESPN will be tracking the latest injuries and updates for your club's players:

Kai Havertz (Arsenal)

Arsenal's Kai Havertz was forced off in the 30th minute of the game between Netherlands and Germany on September 24th with what was described as a muscle injury.

"Both are currently undergoing an MRI," Jurgen Klopp said on RTL about Havertz and Jamal Musiala. "I hope we get the diagnosis [on Thursday] evening. But of course, this isn't great. I hope it's nothing serious. The lads are probably out for us. But hopefully, they'll be back in action relatively quickly."

On September 25 the German Football Association confirmed the attacker would be leaving Klopp's camp and return to Arsenal after suffering what they describe as a 'muscle strain.'

Brian Brobbey (Sunderland)

The powerful Sunderland attacker was also injured in the same game after picking up what looked like a hamstring injury while running for the ball. He immediately went down and signalled to the sideline.

He left the field of his own accord but did have a heavy limp as he walked down the tunnel.

Netherlands boss Xavi Hernandez said after the game: "Brian is indeed injured."

Brobbey was replaced by Joshua Zirkzee in the Dutch squad.

Zion Suzuki (Aston Villa)

The goalkeeper linked up with the Japan squad but according to reports missed the main group training session on September 22nd, according to local reports. Instead he was put on an individual session for a rib injury.

Suzuki was subsequently left out of Japan's matchday squad entirely for Thursday's 3-1 victory over Uruguay.

Dan Ballard (Sunderland)

The Sunderland defender suffered a reported hamstring injury during Northern Ireland's 1-0 victory over Georgia in the UEFA Nations League.

With the score still 0-0 as the match moved into stoppage time, Ballard chased back as Georgia counter-attacked and pulled up clutching the back of his thigh, unable to finish the match in Tbilisi.

Speaking immediately after Friday's match, manager Michael O'Neill said it was too soon to know the extent of his latest injury but will definitely miss the next three Northern Ireland games.

"We'll scan him tomorrow (Saturday), but he's certainly not going to be available for the next three games."

Alexander Isak (Liverpool)

Alexander Isak is returning to Liverpool after sustaining a "minor injury" on international duty.

The striker scored and played the full 90 minutes in Sweden's 2-1 victory over Romania in the Nations League on Friday.

But Isak, who has made a strong start to the season for Liverpool, will not feature in matches against Poland, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Romania over the remainder of the extended international break.

Bruno Fernandes (Manchester United)

The Manchester United midfielder was left out of Portugal's squad for Sunday's game against Norway.

"He played with an injury he brought from Manchester United," Portugal boss Jorge Jesus said. "He really wanted to play against Wales."

Patrick Dorgu (Manchester United)

The news for Manchester United fans who saw Fernandes absent worsened on Sunday when Dorgu was injured.

The left wing-back limped out of Denmark's match against Wales after 30 minutes.

Denmark head coach Brian Riemer told broadcaster TV2 after the game: "He has an injury and has to go home."

Cody Gakpo (Liverpool)

Liverpool forward Gakpo lasted only 17 minutes of the Netherlands' match against Serbia on Sunday. It means Liverpool are sweating over the fitness of Isak and Gakpo.

He looked in pain as he held the lower part of his right leg.

"It's his ankle, that's all I know," Netherlands boss Xavi Hernández said. "Tomorrow we will know, but hopefully it's not too important."

Noussair Mazraoui (Manchester United)

The United full-back was forced out of Morocco's Africa Cup of Nations qualifier against Lesotho after 69 minutes. He was holding his back while on the floor after a challenge.

Nico O'Reilly (Manchester City)

O'Reilly missed England's win against Czechia on Tuesday night after also missing training on Monday. Liverpool winger Rio Ngumoha was called into the matchday squad.

Jan Paul van Hecke (Tottenham Hotspur)

The Tottenham defender Jan Paul van Hecke picked up a foot injury in the Netherlands' clash with Serbia and withdrew from the Netherlands' squad during a training session.

No replacement will be called up for van Hecke. He is now returning to Spurs.

stories.headline: Fernando Alonso refuses to watch F1 from the sofa while he still has 'fire' inside to do better
stories.summary: Fernando Alonso has said he signed for another year of Formula 1 despite knowing 2027 could be just as painful as this year -- but believes an uncompetitive year beats watching races on the sofa at home knowing he could do better.
stories.body:
Fernando Alonso has said he signed for another year of Formula 1 despite knowing 2027 could be just as painful as this year -- but believes an uncompetitive year beats watching races on the sofa at home knowing he could do better.

Alonso, 45, has committed to another year with the struggling Aston Martin team, which will be his 24th in Formula 1.

The two-time champion has been a long-time believer in owner Lawrence Stroll's Aston Martin project, which he dubbed the "team of the future" a few years ago, but it has found itself painfully off the pace with struggling engine partner Honda.

He has also become one of the strongest critics of Formula 1's new hybrid engines, labelling the sport's new era the "battery world championship."

Alonso said he is unsure whether he thinks Aston Martin will improve next year, but he came to the conclusion that he could not walk away just yet.

"I have no guarantees that '27 will be more fun, but it is a commitment that you have to make with yourself," Alonso said. "At the end of the day, I feel fast, I feel motivated, I feel that I am enjoying what I am doing.

"And if I am sitting at home watching TV, watching races, I will feel that I can do better than them. That's what I felt in a way when I was away from F1, I was watching races and I was thinking, 'wow, that start was not right,' I don't know. I was always feeling the fire inside of being there and trying to do better.

"And I still feel it now and I said, until I have that inside, I think it's not time to stop."

After delaying the decision for a few months, Alonso said on Thursday it had been a straightforward call.

"I took the decision quite recently, and sitting with Lawrence it was very straightforward, we didn't have much to discuss," he said. "We both wanted to continue at that point, and it was a five-minute talk and we announced it."

- Why is the Bahrain Grand Prix taking place in Malaysia, 4,000 miles away? F1's unusual race explained

- Ayrton Senna's Honda NSX could fetch £800,000 at London auction

- Esteban Ocon to leave Haas but vows F1 career isn't over

F1 has already confirmed a change to the engine rules next year.

Currently, the engines feature a neat 50-50 split between combustion power and electrical elements, but that is shifting towards 60-40 in favour of conventional combustion power over the next two seasons.

Speaking ahead of the sport's return to Malaysia's Sepang circuit, Alonso admitted the only thing stopping him extending earlier was his feelings about F1's new engines and hinted that the changes might bring about a marked improvement.

"The decision was more about the rules, how enjoyable it is to drive these cars and these rules. We come to an incredible circuit now, it's going to be sad, the middle sector, because we cannot use the battery there.

"If not, you don't have energy for the three consecutive straights, from [Turn] 15 to the last corner, last corner to Turn 1 to Turn 3. You have to use the full 100% battery on those three straights. So the rest is just charging the battery. So that's the problems we are facing now in terms of bringing the cars to the limit on the grip.

"I decided that maybe next year with the 60-40 and with the second year and the rules, maybe there is a better compromise on that. And as I said, let's do it one more time, let's give another opportunity, especially on the power unit side. We started with the wrong foot and it is a question mark what is going to happen next year.

"But I think they deserve another opportunity and I feel blessed."

Alonso had previously taken a sabbatical from F1 in 2019 and 2020, before returning with Alpine in 2021.

In the years leading up to that time away, and during the two years without F1, Alonso won two Le Mans 24 Hours titles with Toyota and took two more cracks at the Indy 500.

When asked if that time away from F1 had helped the longevity of his career since, he said: "Yes, exactly. I had to stop.

"I had to switch off from Formula 1, I had to experience different formulas and different series and different things that I had in my mind. It was a big curiosity and it was great fun to experience all of that. Discover new forms of motorsport, learn from the specialist on each of those series and become a more complete driver.

"That was very important. I still feel that it is appealing. I don't know when I will do it, but I will repeat those experiences."

stories.headline: Fried, Bellinger and García lead Yankees over Red Sox 9-2 for 2-game Wild Card Series sweep
stories.summary: — One year after rallying past the Red Sox to win an AL Wild Card Series, the New York Yankees battered Boston.
stories.body:
NEW YORK -- — One year after rallying past the Red Sox to win an AL Wild Card Series, the New York Yankees battered Boston.


Max Fried dominated the Red Sox in the playoffs for the second straight year, Cody Bellinger and Luis García Jr. homered, and the Yankees rolled to a 9-2 win Wednesday night that completed a two-game sweep.


“We enjoyed tonight. We got a lot more work to do,” Bellinger said.


New York will face AL East champion Tampa Bay in an AL Division Series starting Saturday.


“The fans were electric from the first pitch and the boys were hungry. We got a young, hungry team here," Yankees captain Aaron Judge said as teammates sprayed him with bubbly during the clubhouse celebration. “This makes me feel young every single time.”


Judge missed this series because of a calf injury and isn't sure whether he will play against the Rays, who beat New York 7-6 in the season series.


“Saturday’s a long ways away," he said.


Clinging to a 2-1 lead after Willson Contreras homered to end Boston's 26-inning postseason scoreless streak, the Yankees broke open the game with a six-run sixth after Spencer Jones reached on a wild pitch while striking out leading off — with the help of a video review.


García, acquired at the trade deadline, had three hits in his first postseason start, and Bellinger had four RBI that included a three-run homer capping the sixth-inning burst that put New York ahead 8-1.


“Step one,” said Bellinger, who caught the ceremonial first pitch from his dad, Clay, a 2000 Yankees World Series champion. “Now we got to go into Tampa and play against a tough team."


Boston, which reached the playoffs after rebounding from a 32-46 start, lost last year's wild-card matchup after defeating the Yankees in the opener.


“Regardless of all the special things that happened this summer, and there was quite a few, the goal is to win the World Series and that ended for us tonight, so it’s frustrating,” Red Sox manager Chad Tracy said. “There’s a lot of things you can say, but in the moment right now, I think the guys only care that we lost. And it’s going to take some time to get over that.”


Boston, which also got a seventh-inning homer from Nick Sogard off Will Warren, was missing leadoff hitter Roman Anthony because of a hand injury. The Red Sox were held to a .117 average in the series (7 for 60) with 18 strikeouts and outscored 18-2.


New York hit .382 in the series. Boston's bullpen had a 20.25 ERA.


“We played great baseball in a lot of ways here, obviously anchored by our two great starters," Yankees manager Aaron Boone said.


Yankees batters hit .450 (9 for 20) with runners in scoring position after finishing 19th among the 30 teams with a .246 RISP during the regular season.


“I feel like it’s a whole new level from regular season to these last two days,” Austin Wells said.


A day after Cam Schlittler led New York to a 9-0 win, Fried pitched three-hit ball over six innings to win a postseason game for the first time since the 2021 World Series clincher with Atlanta.


New York started eight left-handed hitters against Sonny Gray, back on the mound where his career derailed during a dismal Yankees stretch in 2017 and ’18.


García's fourth-inning homer put the Yankees ahead and Bellinger, one of the top lefty-on-lefty hitters in the major leagues, added a fifth-inning RBI single against left-handed Erik Miller, who had just relieved.


Gray was disappointed he wasn't allowed to face Bellinger.


“I think I’m the best pitcher in the American League going through the order a third time. I think that’s a fact,” Gray said. "I would’ve liked to live or die with me in that moment, but that's the competitor I am. And, yeah, I think you can probably ask the guys and they felt the same way. So I felt strong. I felt confident. I felt convicted.”


Jones struck out both to start and end the bottom of the sixth, a weird half-inning that included a wild pitch, throwing error, stolen base, bunt single and intentional walk to Ben Rice that preceded Bellinger's homer.


"I can’t believe they were willing to face a guy like Belli with men on base there," Rice said.


Garrett Crochet, who beat the Yankees in last year's Wild Card Series opener, hadn't pitched since April 25 because of left shoulder inflammation when he bounced a sweeper off Adley Rutschman's chest. The catcher picked up the ball and threw to first, where umpire John Libka signaled that Jones was out. The Yankees appealed and the call was reversed by the video umpire at the commissioner's office.


“I couldn’t believe he was there,” Boone said. "I saw the ball squirt away a little bit. I didn’t think that much of it, and looked up and I was, like, 'Oh, he’s safe."


Jones swiped second and kept going to third when Rutschman’s throw skipped into center. Rookie George Lombard Jr. singled for his first postseason RBI, Jazz Chisholm Jr. singled and Trent Grisham loaded the bases with a bunt single.


Wells' sacrifice fly against Garrett Whitlock increased the lead to 4-1, Ryan McMahon hit an RBI groundout and Rice, who had four hits and six RBI in the opener, was intentionally walked. Bellinger reached down and pulled a changeup into the right-center field seats.


Fried struck out six and walked one. He has allowed one run over 12 1/3 innings in the two Wild Card Series against the Red Sox.


“Definitely wasn’t sharp from the get-go but just wanted to challenge them, not try to give any free passes, especially in the first inning," Fried said.


After a night of celebration and a day off, the Yankees will head to Florida on Friday.


“There’s just so much more to do,” Bellinger said after the big night with his father on hand. “So obviously enjoy the moment, understand how cool it is, but keep on going.”


Up Next

New York RHP Gerrit Cole (10-9, 3.61), who would have started a third game against Boston, is likely to start Game 1 against the Rays.

stories.headline: AFL overreactions: Brisbane can't win the 2027 flag without Chris Fagan and Lachie Neale
stories.summary: The season might be over, but there is still plenty to talk about -- particularly at the Lions. Chris Fagan is gone, Lachie Neale is off to Collingwood, and suddenly Brisbane's future looks very different.
stories.body:
The season might be over, but there is still plenty to talk about -- particularly at the Lions. Chris Fagan is gone, Lachie Neale is off to Collingwood, and suddenly Brisbane's future looks very different.

Let's get to this week's overreactions column, where we judge the biggest takeaway as legitimate or irrational.

Brisbane can't win the 2027 premiership without Chris Fagan and Lachie Neale
Beloved Lions coach Chris Fagan revealed to his playing group on Thursday morning that he would be departing the club and drawing the curtain on one of the greatest coaching decades in football history.

Fagan coached Brisbane for 10 seasons and on Saturday afternoon became just the sixth man to lead a team to a premiership three-peat.

The 65-year-old joins dual Brownlow Medal winner Lachie Neale as off-season Lions departures. Earlier in the week, Neale informed the club of his intent to sign with Collingwood as an unrestricted free agent.

Verdict: Overreaction

The losses of Fagan and Neale are obviously immense, and one could argue they were the two most critical pieces to Brisbane's dynastic run. But does anyone really believe this club is now set to nosedive? I didn't think so.

Let's start with Fagan. He leaves behind a Hall of Fame-worthy legacy and some mammoth shoes to fill. But there may not be a club more prepared to fill them than the Lions. Football boss Danny Daly, who has been involved in the AFL for 26 years, is someone that's been both waiting in the wings and long touted as a future senior coach. Should he get the nod, there are many at clubland who believe he can carry on what Fagan has built.

And then there's Neale. Like Fagan, he departs with an all-time resume, but a reminder, he's 33 years of age and probably now behind Will Ashcroft in the club's midfield pecking order. Neale's void isn't one that must be plugged, necessarily, rather it will provide opportunity for others to step up and take on greater responsibility.

Brisbane has already shown it knows how to evolve. This club didn't win three premierships by relying solely on Fagan and Neale. Luke Hodge, for example, helped steady the ship in the early years of Fagan's tenure before the Lions' flag run began. And since then the club has continued to build a deep, talented list.

The Lions might be the second-oldest team on paper, but that's selling short their future. Harris Andrews, Josh Dunkley, Tom Doedee, Jarrod Berry, and Hugh McCluggage are all still on the right side of 30, while Kai Lohmann, Darcy Wilmot, Jaspa Fletcher, Will Ashcroft, Logan Morris, Ty Gallop, Levi Ashcroft, and Daniel Annable are all aged under 24.

The Fagan era is over. The Neale era is over. But that doesn't necessarily mean the Lions' era is, too.

-- Jake Michaels

stories.headline: NFL trade deadline grades: Joey Porter Jr. to Cowboys, J.J. McCarthy to Giants
stories.summary: Can Joey Porter Jr. clean up the Cowboys' defense? Will J.J. McCarthy improve the Giants' QB situation? We're grading NFL trades ahead of November's deadline.
stories.body:
NFL analysts Ben Solak and Seth Walder are grading deals ahead of the 2026 trade deadline, which will pass on Tuesday, Nov. 10, at 4 p.m. ET.

When grading trades, we evaluate them for each team based on on-field impact, cap implications, draft compensation and effects within the context of a team's overall short- and long-term outlooks. How confident are we in knowing if this is a good or bad decision? And how big is the impact of this decision? Both questions play a role in our grades, though a low-impact decision can still receive a strong or poor grade. Even with lower stakes, clear-cut wins or losses still matter.

Here are our evaluations for the first two deals of trading season: J.J. McCarthy to the Giants and Joey Porter Jr. to the Cowboys. Check back right through the deadline for grades on the biggest moves.

Steelers trade CB Porter to Cowboys
Cowboys get: CB Joey Porter Jr.

Steelers get: 2027 sixth-round pick, 2028 second-round pick

Cowboys grade: B

Steelers grade: C+

This is the Cowboys' third trade with the Steelers in the past 18 months (George Pickens and Broderick Jones), and it's their third trade involving a star defensive player after acquiring Quinnen Williams at the trade deadline last season and shipping Micah Parsons to Green Bay last offseason.

It's easy to see what the Cowboys are doing here. DaRon Bland, who first broke onto the scene as a slot corner, was playing on the outside given Dallas' lack of depth. By acquiring Porter, Bland can move back inside, which will allow the Cowboys to relocate 2026 first-round defensive back Caleb Downs, as well. He has been playing the slot, but his natural position is at safety. These are options, not guarantees. Bland might stay outside as the Cowboys instead pursue a strong 1-2 punch at outside corner, with Porter shadowing WR1s.

The salient point is this: Porter can have a rising tide impact on the Cowboys secondary, clarifying the roles of other players and enhancing the whole unit in the process.

Porter is not as tricky of a scheme fit in Dallas as people think, too. His strengths are certainly his length and physicality, such that he can line up in press -- but he has been in press alignments on only 30.6% of his snaps over his career, just above the league average for cornerbacks (24.1%). Porter is a much better man coverage defender than he is in zone, as his passer rating allowed in man coverage over the past four seasons is better than all but Derek Stingley Jr. But the Cowboys are actually running more man coverage (24.8%) under first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker than the league average (23.2%) over the first three weeks.

Of course, early-season rate stats can be noisy. Parker's Vic Fangio-inspired defense will require Porter to play from greater depth than he did in Pittsburgh, and the communication and keys required in that match-heavy system will take some getting used to. But Porter has a valuable and rare skill set in his press-man ability, and premium picks should be spent on players with premium traits. The Cowboys got much, much better in the secondary -- though the move is not without risk.

Acquiring Porter does not solve all their deficiencies; linebacker is still a big problem for this team, and the edge rush isn't far behind. But if the secondary needs less schematic help now that Porter is in play, more coaching tools can be used to hide those other weak spots.

For the Steelers, Porter's recurring back ailments seemed incurable without an extension or a relocation -- what can you do? It's frustrating that GM Omar Khan invested more in third-contract players like Jalen Ramsey and T.J. Watt over a younger, second-contract player like Porter -- Ramsey and Watt will hit their athletic wall far sooner than Porter. Jamel Dean, another third-contract player signed to play corner opposite Porter, now has to cover WR1s alongside Asante Samuel Jr. and 2026 third-round pick Daylen Everette. Corner is no longer a strong position on Pittsburgh's depth chart.

Porter reportedly had contract demands up at the top of the cornerback market, where Devon Witherspoon and Christian Gonzalez recently reset elite deals to clear $33 million annually. I'm not sold that Porter is a top-tier corner deserving of that top money. But because the Steelers let this go on for so long and bleed into the regular season, they were only able to acquire a 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick for a young, ascendent cover corner. They could have -- and should have -- gotten at least a first-round pick by playing this differently and dealing Porter in the spring or earlier in the summer. -- Solak

Vikings trade QB McCarthy to Giants
Giants get: QB J.J. McCarthy

Vikings get: 2027 fifth-round pick

Giants grade: C

Vikings grade: B+

A mere 22 days after the Giants signed Jameis Winston to a two-year, $13 million extension, New York decided it needed to trade a fifth-round pick for an alternative at quarterback. Of course, a lot has happened in three weeks.

Starting quarterback Jaxson Dart suffered a knee injury in Week 2 that is expected to keep him out for at least the regular season. And Winston has delivered two poor performances in Dart's stead, with a 19.0 QBR in relief in Week 2 against the Rams and a 27.9 in Sunday's 12-7 win over the Titans. So in comes McCarthy, the No. 10 pick in the 2024 draft.

McCarthy's pro career has gone poorly so far, which is putting it mildly. He suffered a season-ending knee injury in August 2024, which helped Sam Darnold become Minnesota's starting quarterback. McCarthy was named the starter last season after Darnold departed in free agency but started only 10 games after a series of injuries cost him time. And when he was on the field, the results were not good.

McCarthy posted a 36.1 QBR in 2025 (which ranked 38th out of 45 quarterbacks with at least 100 pass attempts) and recorded a minus-5% pass rate over expected, per NFL Next Gen Stats (43rd out of 45). He threw interceptions at a 4.2% clip (44th), took sacks on 9.4% of dropbacks (40th) and had a 1.8% fumble rate (41st). More alarming is that he did all that while playing for Kevin O'Connell, who has seemingly elevated most of the non-McCarthy quarterbacks he has called plays for.

During training camp, not only did McCarthy lose the Vikings' starting quarterback competition to Kyler Murray, but he then lost the backup competition to Carson Wentz, too. That is a telling red flag.

So why would the Giants trade for him? McCarthy presumably still has some upside based on his draft pedigree, and the Giants are hoping they can profit from him realizing it. But it's hard not to notice the fact that this is John Harbaugh trading for the quarterback his brother, Jim Harbaugh, coached in college at Michigan.

It is difficult to know from the outside which other backup quarterbacks would have been available, but McCarthy still does not seem like an ideal choice. Mac Jones and Spencer Rattler ought to have been the team's first calls (maybe they were). Kirk Cousins probably is off the board with the Raiders sitting at 3-0. Mitchell Trubisky might have been available, considering this already looks like a lost season for Tennessee. And I'm assuming Gardner Minshew II surely must be available, considering he sits in veteran no-man's land between Jacoby Brissett and rookie Carson Beck in Arizona. Stetson Bennett IV could have been an option, too, after the Rams selected Ty Simpson in the first round of this year's draft. I'll grant that some of those options have less upside than McCarthy.

But the Giants' front office should look in the mirror over its bungling of the Winston situation. It's not unreasonable for the Giants to be aggressive in finding a better replacement given how much time is left in the season. But they clearly shouldn't have signed Winston to an extension right before the season if this is how they feel about him!

Even though Murray is a free agent at the end of this season, McCarthy's ship had already sailed in Minnesota after he couldn't beat out Wentz. If he wasn't going to be the Vikings' backup quarterback, his value would likely have continued to drop. To get a fifth-round pick while saving a few million across his remaining 2026 and 2027 compensation (not nothing!) makes sense. They have uncertainty at quarterback in 2027, yes. But that was true whether McCarthy was there or not. -- Walder

stories.headline: Philadelphia Union, USMNT's Cavan Sullivan becomes youngest MLS Player of the Month
stories.summary: Philadelphia Union and USMNT midfielder Cavan Sullivan became the youngest player in MLS history to be named Player of the Month on Wednesday when he was awarded the honors for September.
stories.body:
Philadelphia Union and United States men's national team midfielder Cavan Sullivan became the youngest player in MLS history to be named Player of the Month on Wednesday when he was awarded the honors for September.

At 16, Cavan Sullivan became the youngest player to start a game for the United States since Freddy Adu in 2006 when he was picked in Mauricio Pochettino's XI for Saturday's 4-1 friendly win vs. Peru.

He was one of 11 players -- including seven other teenagers -- to make their first appearances for the U.S. in that game against Peru.

Sullivan, who turned 17 on Sept. 28, came on as a substitute on Tuesday in the USMNT's 4-2 friendly win over Chile.

Sullivan has seven goals and 12 assists in 26 games for the Union, who have surged up to sixth place in the Eastern Conference in recent weeks. He has played 1,675 league minutes in MLS.

His 19 goal contributions are tied with Alphonso Davies (2018) for the second-most by a teenager in an MLS season, trailing only Diego Fagundez (20 in 2013).

Since returning from the World Cup break, the Union have recorded 32 points during a 12-game unbeaten streak, which is tied for the most points by a club in a 12-game span in MLS history. Sullivan has started all 11 of those games, logging a goal contribution in eight of them.

Sullivan and the Union will return after the FIFA international break on Oc. 10 to host Real Salt Lake at Subaru Park (7:30 p.m. ET).

stories.headline: NBA preseason buzz: Latest on trades, news and intel
stories.summary: The NBA regular season is less than a month away, and we're tracking all the news, deals, and trades across the league.
stories.body:
The 2026-27 NBA season officially kicked off Sept. 22 as the Houston Rockets held their media day, before the Dallas Mavericks followed suit Friday.

The other 28 teams in the association joined them Monday, ahead of training camps beginning for most teams.

How will LeBron James and Jaylen Brown look in their new Philadelphia 76ers uniforms? What will Giannis Antetokounmpo's first media day away from Milwaukee look like? And how will the other new faces in new places make their first impressions?

Check back here for all the latest buzz, news and reactions from our ESPN NBA insiders, with the latest info at the top:

Quick links:

Free agency grades | Trade grades

Trade tracker | Transactions | Offseason buzz

Depth charts | Trade machine | More

Sept. 30

Nuggets add Nembhard on two-way deal

Guard Ryan Nembhard has agreed to a two-way contract with the Denver Nuggets, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Nembhard, 23, played 60 games (27 starts) for the Dallas Mavericks in 2025-26 after signing as an undrafted free agent. He was traded to the Atlanta Hawks then to the Charlotte Hornets this offseason before being waived.

Sept. 29

Charania: NBA reviewing finalists' bids for Vegas team

ESPN's Shams Charania reported that the NBA is currently reviewing finalist bids for a new expansion team in Las Vegas. The price range is currently speculated at $12-13 billion with a new arena factored into the cost.

The three final groups are Nancy Walton Laurie and Bill Laurie; Steve Apostolopoulos and Marc Lasry; Bill Foley and Jerry Colangelo, sources told ESPN.

Will KAT take a pay cut in next Knicks deal?

On "NBA Today," ESPN's Malika Andrews detailed Karl-Anthony Towns' mindset toward contract negotiations with the defending champion New York Knicks.

"Towns, from what I have been told, is willing -- similarly to what Jalen Brunson did [but the] numbers aren't the same -- to take a pay cut," Andrews said. "But the pay cut that the Knicks are asking him to take, he views as unreasonable."

Towns, 30, is eligible to sign a four-year, $276 million extension through June 30.

Embiid "full participant" in first Sixers' practice
Joel Embiid was a "full participant all the way through" for the Philadelphia 76ers first practice of training camp, Sixers coach Nick Nurse said Tuesday.

"He looked great," Nurse said of Embiid. "Very, very good news from the standpoint of where it's been the last couple years, last couple summers leading into today. ... It's great to see."

After being named the league MVP in 2023, the 32-year-old center has missed 150 games over the last three seasons because of various injuries.

He also sat out four of the Sixers' 11 playoff games in the spring because of appendicitis, right hip soreness and a right ankle sprain.

The only Sixers player who did not participate in Tuesday's practice according to a team spokesperson was backup big man Adem Bona, who is dealing with a sprained left foot.

Anfernee Simons, who signed a two-year, $12.3 million contract to join Philadelphia in July, said Embiid's presence in the gym was already notable leading up to the start of camp.

"Everybody's been impressed around here about how he's come in and worked," Simons said. "Joel is going to be Joel. He's going to be a dominant player always. We just want to continue for him to be himself, as well, and I think everybody's going to be able to work around that."

Despite the injuries, the 10-year veteran still averaged 26.9 points, 7.7 rebounds, 3.9 assists and 1.2 blocks per game last season.

Embiid's inclusion only added to what several Sixers players described as an "exciting" opening day with LeBron James and Jaylen Brown completing their first official practice with the franchise.

"With any team, we got to start somewhere, and then we got to get better and better, and just keep trying to reach our ceiling, right?" Nurse said. "That happens day-to-day. Can we get up tomorrow, like, 98% as excited as we did today? It's going to be hard to get as excited as we all were today, right?

"But we need to come back, and we need to keep climbing that mountain. That's a daily process. I just want them to reach their potential. If they do, great things are going to happen." -- Dave McMenamin

Hoop Collective: The 2026 NBA Media Day reaction special

Brian Windhorst is joined by ESPN reporters from around the league to check in on Monday's Media Days. Tim MacMahon, Dave McMenamin, Vince Goodwill, Jamal Collier, Anthony Slater and Michael C. Wright all hop on the podcast to discuss the biggest storylines throughout the NBA ahead of training camp.

Topics:

01:08: 76ers Media Day reactions

06:55: How LeBron is assimilating in Philadelphia

15:00: How will the 76ers deploy their talent this year?

18:45: Vibes exceedingly high for the Lakers

32:25: Bronny's quotes about LeBron leaving

1:24:15: Evaluating Kawhi's fit with the Raptors
